newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Analysts' view on S&P upgrade of Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Analysts' view on S&P upgrade of Brazil.

text.p: Following are economists' reactions to the decision by U.S. credit rating agency Standard & Poor's Corp to upgrade Brazil's long-term foreign currency debt rating to BB-minus from B-plus.

MAURO SCHNEIDER, chief economist at ING Bank in Brazil: "This is obviously very good news for the markets and confirms the perception that the political environment for continuing the economic reform program is very favorable."
Schneider said the upgrade also confirms market perception over the past several months that Brazil risk was improving.
THOMAS MALAGA, economist at Brazilian retail bank Unibanco: "I think (S&P) was treating Brazil unjustly in relation to other Latin American countries. The market was expecting this upgrade."
Malaga, however, said Brazil would not see a flood of new investment until it attained BBB, an investment-grade rating.

"If civil service and pension reforms are approved, and with them the possibility of controlling the public deficit, then I think Brazil's rating could rise to BBB... Beginning with BBB, we will be able to see a significant increase in investments to Brazil."

ELENORA SANTOS, economist at Brazilian investment bank Fonte-Cindam: "This has been anticipated for about a month. When S&P visited Brazil last month, they indicated there would be no lowering of the rating."

Still, Santos said the upgrade would improve Brazil's image abroad. "It could lead to better pricing of foreign debt, tighter spreads and it could make it easier for Brazilian corporates to issue abroad."

She added, however, that Brazil had a long way to go to improve its credit rating, noting that Argentina, which is often viewed in the market as an equal credit risk, was still one notch ahead of Brazil.
S&P upgraded Argentina's long-term foreign currency rating on Wednesday to BB from BB-minus.
